dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An equation is hyperbolic when, for every real x and t and every admissible state u, its principal matrix at (x,t,u) has a basis of real eigenvectors with real eigenvalues.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Hyperbolicity concerns all space and time points but only admissible states. The eigenvalues and eigenbasis may depend on x, t, and u.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the admissible-state set from an equation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both constant side states must belong to this set.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the vector-valued forcing function of space, time, and state from an equation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the right-hand side of the algebraic equation and the subtracted term in the residual.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the square real principal-matrix function of space, time, and state from an equation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This matrix acts on qx and is required to have a real eigenbasis at admissible states.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The residual is qt + A(x,t,u) qx - f(x,t,u), with vector operations performed componentwise.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its vanishing is equivalent to qt + A(x,t,u) qx = f(x,t,u), independently of hyperbolicity or admissibility.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: The problem structure contains a governing equation and a function assigning a state to each real spatial point, as exposed by its constructor and projections.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The outer universal quantifier ranges over these equation-and-initial-data objects.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: A problem is jump Riemann precisely when there exist distinct left and right states for which it is Riemann with those states.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The second equivalence unfolds this definition; the final implications classify the constructed problem by equality or inequality of its side states.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: A problem is Riemann precisely when there exist left and right states for which it is Riemann with those states.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The first equivalence expands this existential property and conjoins an always-valid residual identity on its right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: Being Riemann with specified states means the governing equation is hyperbolic, both states are admissible, and the initial data equal the left state for x < 0 and the right state for x > 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the complete conditions on the side-state witnesses without requiring their inequality or restricting the value at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a problem using the given equation and initial data equal to leftState for x < 0, origin for x = 0, and rightState for x > 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The final clause constructs a new problem sharing the original governing equation, with an arbitrary state vector as its value at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the governing equation from a problem.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Determines admissibility, hyperbolicity, the principal matrix, forcing, and the equation retained by the constructed problem.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projects the initial-state function from a problem.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The first characterization constrains this function on the two open half-lines.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: The equation structure contains an admissible-state set, a principal-matrix function, and a forcing function, as exposed by its constructor and projections.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Packages the governing data without a built-in hyperbolicity, regularity, or nonemptiness requirement.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs a problem from an equation and a real-indexed state function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Allows the specified piecewise initial data to be combined with the governing equation without additional hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a square real matrix A, there exist real numbers lambda_p and a basis (b_p) of the full real state space, indexed by the state-coordinate index type, such that A b_p = lambda_p b_p for every p.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Hyperbolicity means diagonalizability over the reals, not distinctness of eigenvalues, orthogonality, or merely reality of the spectrum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: A state-valued function equals a specified left state at every negative real input and a specified right state at every positive real input.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Encodes exact pointwise constancy on open half-lines and leaves the value at zero unrestricted.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: The function selects the left state when x < 0, the right state when x > 0, and the specified origin value otherwise, which over the reals means x = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the initial data for the constructed problem and makes its value at zero independent of both side states.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs an equation from any admissible-state set, principal-matrix function, and forcing function of the stated types.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: No smoothness, openness, nonemptiness, or differential-equation solvability conditions are imposed by construction.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Equality of two objects of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Vector and function equalities are exact and amount to agreement in every coordinate; these are not approximate or almost-everywhere equalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over an object satisfying a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Side states are existential witnesses for each problem; eigenvalues and eigenbases are local witnesses for each principal matrix in the hyperbolicity condition.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type consisting of natural numbers from 0 through n - 1.

dependency_coverage.name: Ne
dependency_coverage.meaning: Inequality is negation of equality.

dependency_coverage.name: Not

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Supplies the real number zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the spatial dividing point and the entries of the residual zero vector.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedCommRing

binders: For every natural number m, set n = m + 1 and V = {0,...,m} → R, identified with R^n.
For every problem P consisting of a governing equation E = (S,A,f) and initial-state function g: R → V, where S ⊆ V, A: R × R × V → R^(n×n), and f: R × R × V → V.
In the first equivalence, left and right states L,R ∈ V are existential witnesses for the fixed problem; these witnesses are fixed across all spatial points.
In the residual equivalence, x,t range independently over all real numbers, and u,qt,qx range independently over all of V. This universal clause lies outside the side-state existential quantifiers.
In the jump equivalence, L,R ∈ V are a separate pair of existential witnesses for the fixed problem.
In the construction clause, L,O,R range universally and independently over V. O is a state value at the spatial origin, not a spatial coordinate.

Within hyperbolicity, for each x,t ∈ R and u ∈ S there exist an eigenvalue family lambda: {0,...,m} → R and an indexed real basis (b_p) of V, with A(x,t,u)b_p = lambda_p b_p for every p. These witnesses may depend on x,t,u.
hypotheses: There are no outer hypotheses on P beyond its type.
The final construction clause assumes E is hyperbolic, L ∈ S, and R ∈ S.
Within that clause, L = R is the premise for the non-jump conclusion, and L ≠ R is the premise for the jump conclusion.
There is no admissibility assumption on O and no assumption that the original initial data g have any particular form.
conclusions: P.IsRiemann if and only if both of the following hold: (a) there exist L,R ∈ V such that E is hyperbolic, L ∈ S, R ∈ S, g(x) = L for every x < 0, and g(x) = R for every x > 0; (b) for every x,t ∈ R and u,qt,qx ∈ V, residual_E(x,t,u,qt,qx) = 0 if and only if qt + A(x,t,u)qx = f(x,t,u).
P.IsJumpRiemann if and only if there exist L,R ∈ V such that P.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R) and L ≠ R.

For every L,O,R ∈ V, if E is hyperbolic and L,R ∈ S, let Q be the problem with governing equation E and initial data h(x) = L for x < 0, h(0) = O, and h(x) = R for x > 0. Then Q.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R), and both implications hold: if L = R then Q is not jump Riemann; if L ≠ R then Q is jump Riemann.
mathematical_definitions: The matrix action is (Av)_i = sum from j = 0 to m of A_ij v_j. Vector addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, and zero are componentwise.
E is hyperbolic precisely when A(x,t,u) is diagonalizable over R for every x,t ∈ R and every u ∈ S, meaning it admits a basis of V consisting of eigenvectors with real eigenvalues.
P.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R) means that E is hyperbolic, L,R ∈ S, g(x) = L for all x < 0, and g(x) = R for all x > 0.
P.IsRiemann means there exist L,R with P.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R). Equality of L and R is permitted.
P.IsJumpRiemann means there exist L,R with P.IsRiemannWithStates(L,R) and L ≠ R.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive finite real state-space dimension and every governing-equation-and-initial-data problem, three assertions hold together. First, the problem is Riemann exactly when it has admissible constant states on the negative and positive half-lines and a governing equation whose principal matrix has a real eigenbasis at every space-time point and admissible state, together with the universal algebraic equivalence between vanishing residual and qt + A qx = f. Second, it is jump Riemann exactly when its Riemann side states can be chosen distinct. Third, for any hyperbolic governing equation from the given problem and any two admissible side states, assigning those states on the respective open half-lines and any state at zero constructs a problem Riemann with those side states. The constructed problem is not jump Riemann when the side states agree and is jump Riemann when they differ.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension is m + 1 with m natural, so it is at least one; zero-dimensional systems are excluded.

Hyperbolicity is required only on S, although A and f are defined on every state. If S is empty, hyperbolicity is vacuous, but no problem can satisfy either Riemann predicate, and the construction clause has no admissible side-state instances.
The initial-state requirements leave g(0) entirely unrestricted. In the constructed problem, O need not belong to S or equal either side state.

When L = R but O differs, the constructed initial data have an isolated discrepancy at zero and still count as Riemann but not jump Riemann. The jump predicate concerns unequal half-line values, not every form of discontinuity.
The half-line equalities hold at every point, not merely almost everywhere. Both real half-lines are nonempty, so they determine their respective constant values uniquely.
The residual equivalence holds for all real x and t, including negative times, and all u,qt,qx ∈ V, including inadmissible u.
qt and qx are arbitrary vectors. No function of space and time is quantified whose derivatives they must be, and no derivative relation is imposed.
The residual equivalence is an algebraic consequence of the residual definition and places no extra restriction on the problem.
Hyperbolicity does not require distinct eigenvalues, a common eigenbasis for different points or states, smooth dependence of eigenvalues or eigenvectors, or uniform bounds on a diagonalization.
No regularity is imposed on A, f, or the admissible-state set. There is no requirement that forcing vanish, that coefficients be constant, or that A arise as the derivative of a flux.
The proposition does not assert existence, uniqueness, regularity, entropy admissibility, weak solvability, or self-similarity of a solution to a differential equation.

The constructed problem retains only the governing equation from P; its initial data replace those of P. The final implication remains conditional if that equation is not hyperbolic or the selected side states are not admissible.
